lines.text: I knelt at the bars. Up close, she was younger than I had thought, and older. Fifteen winters in the dark will do that.
Who are you?
The light in the stone pulsed, slow and heavy, like a heart. Her eyes went far away. For a moment she was only humming again.
Then she came back. It seemed to cost her a great deal.
Not now. There isn't time. When the stones ring, he always comes.
Ilse had reached through the bars to lay her hand on the crystal. Her face went white.
Lucan. The chains go into the stone, and the stone has grown into her. They're one thing now. If we pull her out, we pull out her life.
Then we break the stone.
And kill her that way instead.
It feeds the rings, Lucan. Every glass ring in Aldmere drinks from this. Penhallow's. Stane's. Caddoc's. Break it, and every ring lord in the kingdom goes dark overnight.
And there's something else, underneath. It's holding something. Like a hand pressing a door shut. I can't read what's behind the door.
I didn't care. That's the truth. I would have torn the bars out with my frozen hands. Wren held my arm, and didn't let go.
You'll kill her, Lucan. You know you will.
Ash pushed his great head between the bars, the way he does when he wants his ears scratched.
And she laughed. A small, cracked, surprised laugh, as if she had forgotten how.
She reached out with a thin hand, white with frost, and laid it on his head. Ash closed his eyes.
Something went into him. I felt it through his thread. Warm, and very old.
Then she looked at my hands. White to the wrist. Blue at the fingers. Her face changed.
Keep him warm.
She wasn't talking to me. She was talking to my dog.
When she lifted her hand away, there was frost on Ash's black fur, in the shape of her fingers. It didn't melt.
And behind us, from the dark at the foot of the stair, came a calm, kind voice I knew very well.
She isn't yours to take, Lucan.
